name: security-android-network-security-config-review
intent: Android effective cleartext and trust-anchor policy by build/domain
artifacts: Network Security Config, manifest flags, target SDK, debug/release resources and actual HTTP client.
trace: Resolve which domain/build policy the real client uses, including custom trust managers that bypass declarative configuration.
experiment: Use an emulator and owned local endpoint with synthetic data; compare expected TLS validation and an intentionally invalid test certificate.
disproof: A debug-only trust anchor is not a release flaw; an HTTP string unused by the application is not sensitive cleartext transmission.
repair: Apply correct release/domain trust policy and retest actual client validation and legitimate TLS.
branch_decisions: Resolve build variant, target SDK, domain-config inheritance, debug overrides and the network stack actually making the request. Native or third-party clients may not honor the XML policy. A debug trust anchor is not a release weakness without release applicability; show effective cleartext/peer acceptance with an owned endpoint and the real client path.
